model_interpretation.claim: This remains a one-way 16-byte SIMD-prefix/scalar-suffix hybrid, not T1-style whole-buffer validation. The selected parent locates the first high-bit lane in a mixed vector before calling the scalar decoder. Since that vector starts at a known code-point boundary and the scalar decoder already skips ASCII, starting it at the vector boundary may avoid the mask-shifting lane search at the cost of rechecking at most 15 ASCII bytes. The first high-bit byte remains input to strict validation, including when it is a stray continuation. Prior timings motivate the contrast but do not establish its cause; measure on the official mixed-width n=65536 workload and official ASCII/malformed boundary checks.

This contrasting SIMD-prefix/scalar-remainder hybrid tests whether repeatedly restarting SIMD scans and locating a lane after each decoded code point costs more than it saves. It skips only complete 16-byte ASCII vectors; on the first vector containing any high bit, it sends the suffix from that block boundary to the strict scalar decoder. This avoids assuming the high-bit byte is a lead and preserves bounded loads, but gives up SIMD scanning of later ASCII runs. Measure it on the official mixed-width n=65536 workload; do not infer a speedup from synthetic inputs.

items.objective: Primary hypothesis: vector high-bit scans can skip ASCII spans while the existing strict scalar decoder handles non-ASCII code points. The benefit depends on the actual official mixed-width input containing useful ASCII spans; do not assume this or use synthetic-only results as evidence for the scored workload. Start decoding at a known code-point boundary and treat the first high-bit byte as input to validate—not as an assumed lead, since it may be a stray continuation. Keep loads and tails within n. Preserve exact validity, ABI, output, and thread budget. Measure the official mixed-width n=65536 workload and run the official ASCII/malformed correctness checks, especially for boundaries. Report this approach separately from T1's whole-buffer validation; label any hybrid distinctly and record failed variants.
